Daily Brief

The Middle East conflict escalated sharply on Wednesday as Iran launched ballistic missiles at US bases, prompting joint US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-backed militias in Iraq that killed at least 20 fighters [BBC, Al Jazeera, The Hindu]. The strikes mark a significant development with Saudi Arabia's direct military participation alongside American forces. In Japan, rescue operations continued after a 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Kumamoto, killing at least 13 people and disrupting semiconductor and automotive production at TSMC and Toyota facilities [BBC, Nikkei Asia]. Across southwestern Europe, wildfires have displaced over 330,000 people in France and Spain, with French authorities ordering additional evacuations as a fourth heatwave approaches [France 24, The Hindu, BBC Europe]. Transatlantic tensions deepened as US diplomats walked out of a UN Security Council meeting during French remarks criticizing the Trump administration, while the Pentagon announced a formal review of its European military presence [RFI]. The Trump administration also moved to ban imports of Chinese humanoid robots, citing national security concerns [BBC].

Top Stories
01 Conflict

US and Saudi Arabia Launch Joint Airstrikes on Iran-Backed Militias in Iraq After Iranian Missile Attack

  • Iran's IRGC fired multiple ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East, all of which were intercepted according to US Central Command
  • US and Saudi fighter jets struck logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq belonging to the Popular Mobilisation Forces, killing at least 20 fighters and wounding 32
  • Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed to have struck three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and rejected Oman's proposal for joint regional management of the waterway
  • The PMF described the strikes as a 'dangerous escalation' and 'violation of Iraq's sovereignty'

02 Society

Japan Earthquake Kills 13, Disrupts TSMC and Toyota Production in Kumamoto

  • A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Kumamoto prefecture on Tuesday, reaching maximum intensity of 7 on Japan's seismic scale—the first since the 2024 Noto Peninsula quake
  • At least 13 people confirmed dead with rescue operations ongoing; an explosion occurred at Aeon Mall Kumamoto, trapping multiple people
  • TSMC evacuated personnel from its JASM semiconductor fab; Toyota halted operations at three Fukuoka plants through Friday; Sony and Renesas also paused production
  • Japan Meteorological Agency warned strong aftershocks may continue for up to a week

Wildfires Displace Over 330,000 Across France and Spain as Fourth Heatwave Approaches

  • France ordered 4,000 additional evacuations from Atlantic coast tourist sites; approximately 200,000 people displaced in the Gironde region alone
  • Spain began lifting some evacuation orders, allowing 44,000 people to return home, though Madrid region fires remain the worst in recorded regional history
  • A fourth heatwave expected to bring temperatures to 40°C starting Wednesday, with Spanish meteorological agency warning fire danger will reach 'extreme levels'
  • EU crisis chief stated wildfire response needs more funding and greater focus on forest management as climate change accelerates

04 Geopolitics

US Walks Out of UN Security Council Over French Criticism; Pentagon Launches Europe Troop Review

  • US diplomats walked out of a UN Security Council meeting on Ukraine while French counterparts were speaking, following French criticism of Trump administration human rights record
  • The walkout followed the UN General Assembly's 144-10 vote to reappoint human rights chief Volker Turk despite US opposition
  • Pentagon announced formal review of US military presence in Europe, aiming to accelerate NATO's transition to Europe taking 'primary responsibility for its conventional defense'
  • Tensions compound broader US-Europe disputes over NATO burden sharing, troop deployments, and Trump's stated interest in Greenland

Trump Administration Bans Imports of Chinese Humanoid Robots Citing National Security

  • FCC banned new imports of foreign-made humanoid robots and four-legged machines, with most affected products made in China
  • Ban also covers power inverters used in data centers and solar panels, citing risks of remote shutoff, data theft, and surveillance by 'foreign government actors'
  • Items added to FCC's Covered List; existing authorized models can still be sold and imported
  • Chinese embassy accused US of 'politicising' trade issues and imposing sanctions based on 'groundless pretexts'
